dedupe_keys.name: future uk material demand for key decarbonisation technologies bgs to 2050

description: This dataset holds the end results of scenario-based modelling of future UK demand for raw materials used in decarbonisation technologies: batteries, electrolysers, fuel cells, heat pumps, nuclear, photovoltaics, traction motors and wind turbines. The National Geoscience Data Centre page says the models project material demand to 2050 from government targets, future energy scenarios, evolving technologies, material intensities and efficiencies, and links the foresight reports of the UK Critical Minerals Intelligence Centre, including an overview (OR/24/005) and case studies on traction motors, wind turbines, batteries and photovoltaic cells. It was published on 26 February 2025 by Evi Petavratzi and Pierre Josso of the British Geological Survey in Excel format, downloadable from the NGDC accessions service, free under the Open Government Licence with a NERC acknowledgement. Coverage is national for the UK. Caveats: the results depend on the chosen scenarios and material intensities, the page gives no spatial detail, and the exact materials and number of scenarios are not stated on the page read. For simulation it gives material demand paths for supply security and import dependence scenarios of the UK energy transition, and inputs for linking energy system plans to mineral supply chains. Related catalogue records include the BGS UK Minerals Yearbook, the BGS World Mineral Statistics and the USGS world minerals outlook to 2029.
